8 Unit 2 · Differentiation — Definition and Fundamental Properties Foundational [1 mark]
The graph of a differentiable function f(x)f(x)f(x) is shown below. Which of the following statements about the derivative of f(x)f(x)f(x), denoted f′(x)f'(x)f′(x), at x=1x = 1x=1 is true?
A. f′(1)f'(1)f′(1) cannot be determined from the graph.
B. f′(1)f'(1)f′(1) is zero.
C. f′(1)f'(1)f′(1) is negative.
D. f′(1)f'(1)f′(1) is positive.
Correct Answer: (D) — f′(1)f'(1)f′(1) is positive.
The derivative of a function at a point represents the slope of the tangent line to the graph of the function at that point. Observing the graph at x=1x = 1x=1, the function f(x)f(x)f(x) has a positive slope. Therefore, f′(1)f'(1)f′(1) is positive. A negative slope would indicate a decreasing function, and a zero slope would indicate a horizontal tangent line.
9 Unit 7 · Differential Equations Foundational [1 mark]
Consider the differential equation dydx=kx−3\frac{dy}{dx} = kx - 3dxdy​=kx−3, where kkk is a constant. The graph of a particular solution y=f(x)y = f(x)y=f(x) to this differential equation is shown below. The tangent line to the graph at x=1x=1x=1 has the equation y=−2x+5y = -2x + 5y=−2x+5. Find the value of kkk.
A. 111
B. −1-1−1
C. −3-3−3
D. 333
Correct Answer: (B) — −1-1−1
The differential equation is dydx=kx−3\frac{dy}{dx} = kx - 3dxdy​=kx−3. \\ The given tangent line at x=1x=1x=1 is y=−2x+5y = -2x + 5y=−2x+5. \\ The slope of the tangent line at x=1x=1x=1 is dydx∣x=1\frac{dy}{dx} \Big|_{x=1}dxdy​​x=1​. From the equation of the tangent line, the slope is −2-2−2. \\ Thus, dydx∣x=1=−2\frac{dy}{dx} \Big|_{x=1} = -2dxdy​​x=1​=−2. \\ Substituting x=1x=1x=1 into the differential equation, we get dydx∣x=1=k(1)−3=k−3\frac{dy}{dx} \Big|_{x=1} = k(1) - 3 = k - 3dxdy​​x=1​=k(1)−3=k−3. \\ Equating the two expressions for the slope at x=1x=1x=1: k−3=−2k - 3 = -2k−3=−2. \\ Solving for kkk: k=−2+3=1k = -2 + 3 = 1k=−2+3=1. \\ Therefore, the value of kkk is 1. \\ Common errors: \\ 1. Incorrectly using the y-intercept of the tangent line. \\ 2. Confusing the derivative with the function value.
